card: This PR updates estimatesmartfee to fall back to the block policy fee estimator when the mempool policy estimator cannot produce an estimate, rather than returning an error. It also notifies the fee estimator to clear tracked mined-block stats if loading mempool.dat fails or is disabled at startup, preventing the estimator from returning an artificial fee floor on an empty mempool. In addition, it renames the default fee_rate_estimator parameter from 'none' to 'auto' and rejects unknown values. These changes ensure fee estimation remains available during mempool stats gathering and avoids inaccurate estimates from stale state. This work is extracted from #36182 and marked for backport to 32.x.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided; commits and functionality remain unchanged from the previous description.
evidence: PR description: 'Falls back to the block_policy fee rate estimator when mempool_policy is not available. This preserves the previous behavior and lets users who update their node keep using block_policy estimates until the mempool policy has finished gathering stats and is ready to serve estimates.'

Commit 5b77288673: 'When the mempool fails to load at startup (persistence disabled, or a missing or corrupt mempool.dat), init notifies the fee_rate_estimator_man, which clears its tracked mined-block window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node no longer has and, once the mempool refilled, serve an estimate built on it.'

Commit 4056908f0f: '"none" read as though fee estimation was disabled, so rename the public value... Also reject unknown fee_rate_estimator values instead of silently coercing them to the default, so a mistyped value surfaces an error.'
problem: When the mempool policy fee estimator lacks sufficient block data or coverage, estimatesmartfee returned an error instead of using available block policy estimates, degrading availability after node restarts or upgrades. Additionally, if mempool.dat failed to load or persistence was disabled, the mempool estimator retained mined-block statistics that could falsely indicate a healthy empty mempool and return the fee rate floor.

risk.why: Defects in estimator fallback logic or RPC option handling could cause estimatesmartfee to fail or return inaccurate fee rates, leading to stuck transactions or overpaying fees.

summary: Falls back to the block policy fee rate estimator when the mempool policy estimator cannot produce an estimate, rather than returning an error. Clears the mempool estimator's tracked mined-block stats when loading the mempool from disk fails or is disabled at startup. In estimatesmartfee, renames the default fee_rate_estimator option from 'none' to 'auto' and rejects unknown option values with an RPC error.
